title: Compact, resilient layout rules for console tables, charts, and modals across browsers
creator: Priya Mehta
description: Goal: define and prototype a small set of layout rules and fallbacks that make key Console pages (dashboards, rollout screens, and cost views) behave predictably across viewport widths and major browsers, including Safari/iOS and older Edge. This ticket covers: table density and truncation rules, chart micro-layout behavior (sparklines and histogram cards), modal stacking and safe-area handling, and rollouts/canary list responsiveness. We want a single doc + prototype that engineers can implement with minimal custom media query spaghetti and that degrades gracefully when feature queries fail or browser bugs occur.
acceptance_criteria: No horizontal overflow at breakpoints: 320px, 375px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px when viewing representative pages (dashboard card grid, rollout list with filters, cost breakdown table)
Tables: long cell content truncates with ellipsis and a keyboard-focusable tooltip that shows full text; at <= 480px certain low-priority columns hide according to token rules
Charts: sparkline and histogram cards maintain legible axis marks at small widths and switch to summarized numbers when space < 200px
Modals: center on desktop, inset to top sheet on small touch devices; respect safe-area-inset on iOS and avoid positioning bugs caused by transform on ancestors
Rollouts: canary variant list keeps action buttons accessible (stack vertically on mobile) and retains keyboard order
Cross-browser parity: behaviour validated on latest Chrome, Firefox, Safari (macOS+iOS), and Edge; documented known deviations and workarounds
Automated visual regression tests are added for the representative snapshots and a short Playwright e2e asserts layout and keyboard focus
Performance: avoid layout thrashing patterns; use will-change conservatively and prefer composited transforms only where measured improvement occurs
design_notes: Use a grid-first approach for card layouts with a feature query fallback to flexbox for browsers that lack grid gap support. Document exact token values for gutters and breakpoints so engineers can reuse console tokens.
Define three table density presets (comfortable, compact, condensed) and a simple rule: switch to compact below 1024px, condensed below 768px unless user preference sets density explicitly.
For truncation, use 'text-overflow: ellipsis' + an accessible tooltip element that appears on hover and focus (aria-describedby). Tooltip should be visible on touch by long-press fallback.
Charts: prefer canvas for large datasets for perf but render micro-sparklines with svg for crispness at small sizes; supply fallback static PNG for legacy iOS versions that mishandle SVG transforms.

Modal stacking: adopt a z-index scale and avoid nested transform contexts that break position: fixed. Where an ancestor must be transformed, switch modal to position: absolute and re-calc on resize/scroll via a minimal JS shim.
Safe-area: utilize env(safe-area-inset-*) for top/bottom offsets on mobile; test on device or simulator rather than only desktop responsive mode.
Keyboard focus: ensure tables, charts (if interactive), and modals have clear focus states and tab order; escape key closes modal; focus returns to trigger element on close.
Rollouts page: action menu should degrade to inline action buttons if popover is clipped on smaller viewports.

Cost views: token-level breakdown cards should collapse numeric columns into an expandable row on small screens to avoid horizontal scrolling. Expand/collapse must be accessible and preserved through navigation state when possible.
decisions: Adopt CSS Grid primary layout with explicit fallback to Flexbox using '@supports (display: grid)' checks — approved by eng during sync on 2025-02-20
Prefer SVG sparklines for single-value cards; use a server-side generated PNG fallback only for iOS 12/13 where inline SVG transforms are buggy
Modal top-sheet pattern used for < 540px viewports; centered modal for >= 540px. Implementation note: use a small runtime check to toggle 'data-modal-mode' when safe-area insets are present
Sticky column in tables enabled for desktop only; turned off on mobile to avoid layout thrash and clipping
Virtualized table rendering will be behind a feature flag that can be toggled per route — engineering to add flag: 'table-virtualization'
prs: GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2782 (initial grid -> flex fallback styles)
